subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Magnetic and Electric Forces Without Touching

items.prompt:
Magnets can push or pull other magnets
A) only when touching
B) across a gap without touching
C) never
D) only underwater
items.answer: B) across a gap without touching

items.prompt:
Two magnets that push apart are
A) attracting
B) repelling
C) touching
D) melting

A balloon rubbed on hair picks up paper bits using
A) a magnetic metal
B) a static electric force
C) glue
D) sound

A magnet pulls a paper clip harder when the magnet is
A) farther away
B) closer
C) turned off
D) painted

steps: The magnetic force is stronger at closer distances.

items.prompt:
Which object will a magnet most likely pick up?
A) A plastic button
B) A steel nail
C) A rubber band
D) A paper cup

steps: Magnets attract certain metals like steel.

items.prompt:
As two magnets move farther apart, the force between them gets
A) stronger
B) weaker
C) exactly the same
D) louder

steps: More distance means a weaker force.

items.prompt:
Which is a good cause-and-effect question about magnets?
A) What color is the magnet?
B) Does a magnet pull harder when it is closer?
C) Who owns the magnet?
D) Is the magnet pretty?
items.answer: B) Does a magnet pull harder when it is closer?

steps: This asks how a cause (distance) affects an effect (pull).

items.prompt:
Two magnets repel. If you flip one around, they will
A) still repel
B) attract
C) disappear
D) become plastic

steps: Flipping a magnet changes repelling into attracting.
